lines.text: Commenters swear a jar of gas vapor can get a car hundreds of miles per gallon so he tests it on a mower.
beats: ai:silver sedan cruising on an empty desert highway at sunset

lines.text: But if that worked every car maker would have switched to vapor years ago.
beats: ai:modern car factory assembly line with robotic arms welding car bodies

lines.text: So he blocks the fuel line and seals the gas container with JB Weld so only vapor reaches the engine.
The engine sucks air down 2 pipes into the gas which bubbles into vapor and a valve feeds it in.
And to his surprise it fires up and runs the mower on pure vapor.
Which makes sense because gas has to become vapor to burn anyway and a carburetor already does that job.
beats: ai:macro of fine gasoline mist spraying inside the throat of a small engine carburetor

lines.text: Then both setups get the same fuel and the vapor jar runs 27 and a half minutes while the normal tank dies at 26 minutes 47 seconds.
So vapor only buys 43 extra seconds which is 2 to 3 percent and nowhere near hundreds of miles per gallon.
Because the energy is locked inside the gasoline so turning it into vapor can't magically create more.
beats: ai:single drop of gasoline glowing with warm light falling into a pool macro

lines.text: He went from skeptic to believer but would you trust a vapor jar in your car?

facts_checked: Transcript IuGWHfWqWtg + scan frames: commenters claim engine on gas vapor -> hundreds of mpg vs 20-30 (0:26-0:38); Todd: car makers would have switched years ago (0:13-0:26); JB Weld seals container (2:13-2:30, frames 2:12-2:30); fuel line blocked off (2:32-3:19, caption 3:03 'Fuel tank is not needed', caption 6:15 'Fuel line is blocked off'); how it works: engine vacuum draws air down two pipes into fuel, bubbles -> vapor -> single line -> valve -> engine (3:41-4:47, Todd pointing 4:15-4:48); valve close-up 5:54; bubbling jar 6:03-6:36; engine runs on vapor and mower driven across lawn (5:00, 6:45-7:18); fuel economy test: vapor ran 27.5 min (9:58, caption 9:24 'Engine ran for 27.5 minutes, but did not use all fuel'), same amount of fuel (blue tape line) in normal tank ran out at 26 min 47 s (caption 11:15/11:18); difference 43 s = ~2.7% (our calc), caption 11:36 'Only 2-3% fuel savings at most'; claims of 400-500% savings not seen (11:36-11:47); 'came in a total skeptic and now I'm a believer' (11:24-11:32). Gasoline must vaporize to burn and carburetor atomizes fuel; vaporizing does not add chemical energy (standard combustion physics, our commentary).
